title: quant-kernel-coalescer-and-kv-aware-scheduler-for-low-latency-quant-inference
author: Samir Patel
release_notes: Introduces a kernel coalescer that reduces GPU kernel launch overhead for short token spans and a KV-cache-aware scheduler that prioritizes requests with warm KV state. Expect 8-18% median p50 latency improvement on small-sequence INT8 and FP8 workloads; no API changes.
description:
Motivation: small-sequence, high-QPS workloads see disproportionate kernel-launch and scheduling overhead when using quantized execution paths (INT8/FP8 + smoothquant). This patch introduces a lightweight kernel coalescer and a KV-cache-aware scheduling policy to reduce per-request latency without sacrificing throughput. The change also fuses the dequantization step for smoothquant-adapted kernels when safe, reducing memory copies and extra kernel launches.

What changed: 1) kernel_coalescer: a runtime component that groups adjacent short kernels (typically per-head or per-MLU micro-op) at the launch layer into a single compound kernel invocation when the combined tensor shapes fit optimized microkernel tiling heuristics; 2) kv_aware_scheduler: scheduler scoring now includes a KV-warmth factor (cache hit rate + last-access recency) to prefer colocating requests that will reuse KV state on the same worker, reducing remote KV fetch latency; 3) dequant_fusion: added guarded fusion for smoothquant dequant->matmul->requant sequences for INT8/FP8 paths, with a verified fallback to existing separated path on mismatch; 4) continuous_batcher tweaks: token-aware microbatching with reduced padding amplification for mixed-length quantized requests; 5) telemetry & flags: feature flags to enable/disable coalescer and fusion per-customer, expanded histograms for kernel launch counts, per-request KV-warmth logging.

Compatibility & safety: Fusion is guarded by shape/scale checks and a per-model capability flag added to the model manifest. If runtime detects incompatible layout or scale drift (via a cheap sample check), it falls back to the original dequant path and emits a one-time regression telemetry event. The scheduler change is additive and can be toggled with the runtime.scheduling.kv_warmth weight. No changes were made to public APIs.

Benchmarks: microbenchmarks were run on p4d and A100 pools against a mix of short-sequence chat workloads (avg tokens/request 8), long-sequence generation (avg 512), and mixed-ratio traffic. Results: median p50 latency for INT8 short-sequence workloads improved 12% p50 and 9% p99; FP8 saw 8% p50 and 6% p99 improvements. End-to-end host CPU overhead reduced by 6% due to fewer kernel launches. Workload-specific caveats included a small throughput regression (1-2%) on extreme long-sequence-only synthetic cases when coalescer heuristics were enabled; heuristics default to conservative settings and can be tuned per deployment.

Testing: unit tests for kernel coalescer heuristics, scheduler scoring, and guarded fusion paths were added. Integration tests run in the perf-canary lab against the quant suite and KV cache stress harness. A small flake in dynamic-batcher was observed and rerun in CI.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout starting with dedicated clusters and canary customers; monitor kernel.launches, kv.cache_hit_rate, latency.P50/P99, and dequant.fallback_rate. If dequant.fallback_rate > 0.5% for a model, automatically revert kernel fusion for that model.

Related: builds on prior work for batching and prefetch in ENG-1320 and smoothquant tuning in ENG-1182. Linked Linear tickets: ENG-1429 (coalescer), ENG-1473 (scheduler).

notes_for_oncall: If several models surface >0.5% dequant.fallback_rate, rollback fusion via runtime flag and notify infra. KV-warmth should not be increased beyond default weight without observing stable cache hit-rate > 20%.

runtime: add kernel coalescer and KV-aware scheduling for quant paths (INT8/FP8); guarded smoothquant dequant fusion
Performance: median p50 latency improvement for short-sequence quant workloads (8-18%)
